synopsis: ISO 21815 is the core off-road collision-warning and avoidance family: Part 1:2022 covers detection, warnings, automatic intervention and tests for earth-moving, mobile underground-mining and road-construction machinery; intervention is limited to speed reduction, stopping or motion inhibition, not automatic steering [f2055, f5156, f5909]. Part 2:2021 supplies the J1939 intervention interface, confirmed in December 2024, while Part 3:2023 covers forward/reverse risk areas, builds avoidance distance from detection, decision, action, stopping and safety-distance components, and places intervention at risk level 4 or above [f2057, f5158, f6680, f5912]. As of 1 October 2026, Part 4 was under publication for October and Part 5 was at proof stage for November; Part 4 addresses swing/rotation mainly by preventing motion from starting and expressly excludes avoidance by automatic brake application, so later users should re-check catalogue status [f49, f50, f11423, f7543, f55]. The family supplies physical test procedures, including performance pass/fail and false-positive tests, but the corpus found no rules establishing acceptable simulation evidence or virtual-only validation, and the listed standards do not supply a statistical acceptance target [f7726, f8321, f9459, f324]. Standardized intervention does not establish quantified field effectiveness or second-order hazards, public previews supplied no human reaction model, and safe-operation responsibility remains with the operator [f3443, f3493, f10874]. For planning, ISO 21815 and EMESRT scenarios anchor the validation test space; a program starting in October 2026 could realistically have an operating-domain definition and scenario catalogue working by mid-2027, with interoperability demonstrated through the Part 2 interface and common site products [f6641, f63, f10726].

relations.note: Both report Part 4 under publication in October 2026.
Catalogue stage and edition details restate Part 4 publication status.
Unfinished publication status motivates later catalogue checks.
Both describe rotation prevention primarily through inhibition before motion starts.
Explicit exclusion of automatic braking sharpens the rotation-inhibition scope.
Both describe Bell E-series third-party Level 9 integration through a Part 2 gateway.
The HIL bench can emulate the specified slow, stop and inhibit commands.
Both identify Part 2 as the J1939 braking interface.
Both construct risk distance from processing times, stopping distance and a safety margin.
Both describe Part 3 forward/reverse avoidance through slowing, stopping or motion inhibition.
Both identify Part 3 coverage of forward and reverse risk areas.
Both retain safe-operation responsibility with the operator under Part 3.
Both describe collision avoidance through speed reduction and stopping.
Details the physical test conditions, performance criteria and false-positive test specified by clause 6.
Absence of virtual-only wording reinforces the unresolved allowance for virtual testing.
Missing human reaction models underpin limits on predicting fatigued responses to nuisance warnings.
Established scenario anchors support the proposed mid-2027 operating-domain and catalogue milestone.
Example stopping calculations assist distance construction but are not themselves a validation method.
